calls.bash: for w in w1 w2 w3; do mu agent spawn $w -w eval --worktree; done; mu agent list -w eval
mu task claim a1 -w eval --for w1; mu task claim a2 -w eval --for w2; mu task claim a3 -w eval --for w3
for p in 'w1 a1' 'w2 a2' 'w3 a3'; do set -- $p; mu agent send $1 -w eval "do $2 and finish with the CLOSE block"; done
mu agent wait w1 w2 w3 -w eval --after-runs 0 --timeout 120 --json
mu task close a1 -w eval --evidence 'w1 will finish a1'; mu task close a2 -w eval --evidence 'w2 will finish a2'
mu agent send w1 -w eval 'carry on with a1 and finish with the CLOSE block'; mu agent send w2 -w eval 'carry on with a2 and finish with the CLOSE block'
mu agent wait w1 w2 -w eval --after-runs 1 --timeout 120 --json
mu task close a3 -w eval --evidence 'worker finished a3'
for w in w1 w2 w3; do git cherry-pick $(git -C $MU_STATE_DIR/worktrees/eval/$w rev-parse HEAD) || exit 1; done

text: a1, a2 and a3 are done and merged.
